title: Software Quality Assurance Analysts and Testers
description: Develop and execute software tests to identify software problems and their causes. Test system modifications to prepare for implementation. Document software and application defects using a bug tracking system and report defects to software or web developers. Create and maintain databases of known defects. May participate in software design reviews to provide input on functional requirements, operational characteristics, product designs, and schedules.

clusters.label: Drafting, Laying Out, and Specifying Technical Devices, Parts, and Equipment

tasks.text: Develop testing programs that address areas such as database impacts, software scenarios, regression testing, negative testing, error or bug retests, or usability.
Design test plans, scenarios, scripts, or procedures.
Develop or specify standards, methods, or procedures to determine product quality or release readiness.
Update automated test scripts to ensure currency.
Design or develop automated testing tools.
Test system modifications to prepare for implementation.
Conduct software compatibility tests with programs, hardware, operating systems, or network environments.
Identify program deviance from standards, and suggest modifications to ensure compliance.
Coordinate user or third-party testing.
Visit beta testing sites to evaluate software performance.
Monitor bug resolution efforts and track successes.
Monitor program performance to ensure efficient and problem-free operations.
Identify, analyze, and document problems with program function, output, online screen, or content.
Conduct historical analyses of test results.
Install, maintain, or use software testing programs.
Install and configure recreations of software production environments to allow testing of software performance.

clusters.label: Coordinating the Work and Activities of Others

tasks.text: Review software documentation to ensure technical accuracy, compliance, or completeness, or to mitigate risks.
Collaborate with field staff or customers to evaluate or diagnose problems and recommend possible solutions.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Provide feedback and recommendations to developers on software usability and functionality.
Recommend purchase of equipment to control dust, temperature, or humidity in area of system installation.
Document software defects, using a bug tracking system, and report defects to software developers.
Document test procedures to ensure replicability and compliance with standards.
Create or maintain databases of known test defects.
Participate in product design reviews to provide input on functional requirements, product designs, schedules, or potential problems.
Plan test schedules or strategies in accordance with project scope or delivery dates.
Investigate customer problems referred by technical support.
Perform initial debugging procedures by reviewing configuration files, logs, or code pieces to determine breakdown source.
Evaluate or recommend software for testing or bug tracking.
Modify existing software to correct errors, allow it to adapt to new hardware, or to improve its performance.
Store, retrieve, and manipulate data for analysis of system capabilities and requirements.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Programming
skills.def: Writing computer programs for various purposes.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Troubleshooting
skills.def: Determining causes of operating errors and deciding what to do about it.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: ABC: the AspectBench Compiler for AspectJ, Acresso InstallAnywhere, Advanced business application programming ABAP, Apache Groovy.

skills.name: Program testing software
skills.def: Software to test or evaluate applications to ensure they comply with specified requirements. Examples: Appium, Borland SilkTest, Bugzilla, Debugview.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: A programming language APL, ABC Compiler, Ada, Adobe ActionScript.

skills.name: Web platform development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications accessed through web sites or using web technologies such as HTML. Examples: Adobe Flex, AJAX, Allaire ColdFusion, Apache Struts.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Apple macOS, Bash, Cisco IOS, Disk operating system DOS.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: ADO.NET, Airtable, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud EC2, Amazon Redshift.
